what_its_for: Estazolam is a sleep medicine (sedative) used to help you fall asleep and stay asleep through the night. It is meant for short-term use only, usually no longer than 1 to 2 weeks.
how_to_take: Take estazolam by mouth as a tablet, only at bedtime and only when you have a full 7 to 8 hours available to sleep. Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. You may take it with or without food, but avoid taking it right after a heavy, high-fat meal as this may slow how quickly it works. Only take one dose per night — never take an extra dose if you wake up in the middle of the night.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 mg at bedtime. Your doctor may increase this to 2 mg if needed. Older adults or people who are smaller in size usually start at a lower dose of 0.5 mg. Always follow exactly what your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: Estazolam is only taken when needed at bedtime, so a traditional missed dose does not apply. If you forget to take it at bedtime and it is still nighttime with at least 7 to 8 hours left before you need to wake up, you may take it then. If it is almost time to wake up, skip the dose entirely. Never double up on doses.
storage: Store estazolam at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a safe place out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any unused tablets safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT drink alcohol while taking estazolam — this combination can be very dangerous and even life-threatening. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires full alertness the morning after taking estazolam, as you may still feel drowsy. Avoid taking other sleep aids, anti-anxiety medicines, opioid pain medicines, muscle relaxers, or antihistamines unless your doctor has approved them. Do not take grapefruit or grapefruit juice as it may increase the amount of medicine in your blood. Do not stop taking estazolam suddenly without talking to your doctor, especially if you have been taking it for a while.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: doing activities while asleep that you do not remember (sleep-walking, sleep-driving, cooking, or eating while not fully awake); unusual changes in mood or behavior such as aggression, confusion, or thoughts of harming yourself; memory problems or feeling like you cannot think clearly; signs of allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; feeling like you need to take higher doses for it to keep working; or difficulty breathing or very slow, shallow breaths. Also call your doctor if your sleep problems do not improve after 7 to 10 nights.
when_it_works: Estazolam usually starts working within 15 to 30 minutes after you take it. That is why you should only take it right when you are ready to go to sleep. It is intended for short-term use only (1 to 2 weeks). If you still have sleep problems after this time, talk to your doctor about other options.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): You are more sensitive to the effects of this medicine. You are at higher risk of falls, confusion, and memory problems. A lower starting dose is recommended, and this medication is generally not preferred for older adults. Pregnant women: Estazolam can harm an unborn baby and should NOT be used during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding mothers: This medicine may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. Do not breastfeed while taking estazolam. Children and teenagers: This medicine is not approved for use in people under 18 years old. People with liver or kidney disease: Your body may process this medicine more slowly, increasing side effects. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose.
